ov: Winged insects with large, often brightly coloured wings, around 18,500 species in all. Each starts as a caterpillar, pupates in a chrysalis, and emerges as an adult that sips nectar through a long, coiled proboscis.
df: Adults sip nectar from flowers. Caterpillars eat the leaves of the plants their eggs were laid on.

cf.tip: Butterflies fly by day, have clubbed antennae and rest with wings held upright. Most moths fly at night, have feathery or tapering antennae, and rest with wings flat.

fx: Some, like the monarch and the painted lady, migrate over long distances.
